newsitem.title: LATVIA: ANALYSIS-RESULTS FLOOD FAILS TO BOOST LATVIAN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS-RESULTS FLOOD FAILS TO BOOST LATVIAN MARKET.

text.p: First-half corporate results were in line with or better than expectated but are unlikely to spark better activity before the autumn, analysts said on Friday.
The slew of results has failed to interrupt the holiday-period lull but issues by leading bank Unibanka and Balta insurance firm showed dormant potential.
Investors, both local and foreign, have been conspicuous by their absence during the summer but were expected to return as the holiday period comes to an end.
"The (corporate) results in general are good, for some even better than planned," said Juris Kimmelis, Unibanka analyst.
"That includes Valmiera Glassfibre , Transport Fleet , Lode Brick , to a certain extent Daugavpils Chain ," he said.
The main event of the week was the auction of one million shares in Unibanka. The issue by insurer Balta also caught the attention as it was oversubcribed 70 times.

"The (Unibanka) auction result caused a rise in interest in securities, including among medium-sized investors, however it will be difficult to move it (the market) as the market has been stagnating for a long time," Rietumu Bank securities dealer Dmitry Krutik said in his weekly bulletin.
In terms of results, Unibanka, Staburadze and Kaija cannery had H1 profits in line with expectations while RTF and Jekabpils Sugar beat expectations.

"The market is still slightly cautious about both RTF and Riga Shipyard, whose good first-half year 1996 was not supported by the annual result, which was an unpleasant surprise," said Girts Ozols, Hansbank-Latvija dealer.
"RTF's price could be higher, as it is a profitable business but investors are fed up with a certain lack of transparency," Parekss dealer Leonid Ruderman said.
Jekabpils Sugar's half million lats six-month profit outperformed all forecasts, dealers said.
"The cyclical nature of the business and concerns over Jekabpils liquidity, however, put a dampener on buying interest, despite its high p/e ratio," Ozols said.
Jekabpils price earnings ratio is currently close to two, compared to an average on the official list of 10.
Analysts said that jumps in the price of several stocks after the first-half results were due mainly to professional players rather than long-term investors.
Some analysts said planned improvements in the current trading system was a factor that could influence activity.
"If the bourse came to a continuous quotation system, the impact would be significant," Hansabank's Ozols said. "This should be matter of the second half of the year."
The bourse has embarked on a trading modernisation programme aimed at bringing it at some point to continuous trading at least with several of the most liquid stocks.
The market has also been encouraged by the disclosure level of listed companies after the bourse introduced its free list in July, dealers and analysts said.
"The free list is also generating good results, especially among forestries, to start with Saldus," Kimmelis said. "Their drawback unfortunately is their small size," he added.
